column1: # level 0 = THE NORTH ROAD, built 2026-08-30 for the patrol.
# NOT the DMG wilderness tables, which are built for open country and would put
# a 50-orc warband on a trade road two hours from a market town. This table is
# scoped to the PLACE, not to the party's level: a settled road inside a day of
# a town that has farms on it, a reeve, and a weekly market. If that road
# routinely held warbands the town would not be there.
# It is not toothless -- 3 and 6 can kill somebody on 2 hit points -- but the
# ceiling is set by geography rather than by mercy, which is the distinction
# that matters. Roll 1 in 6 per half-day of patrolling.

column3: entry
Travellers on foot (2-5) — a family, a pedlar, a pair of drovers. Not a fight; they are frightened of YOU until spoken to. Reaction roll.
Sign only — a cold campfire off the verge, old boot-marks in a ditch, a cut strap in the grass. Days old. Nothing to fight, something to read.
Wolves (2-5) — AC 7, HD 2+2, #AT 1, D 2-5, MV 180' (60'), Save F1, ML 8 (MM). THE DANGEROUS ENTRY. Will not press a large armed group that stands its ground; morale breaks fast.
A merchant's cart with 1-2 hired guards. Wary, then relieved. Good for the party's reputation and it TALKS in town afterward.
Nothing at all. A day of walking. This is the commonest real outcome and it is the one that proves the road is clear.
Desperate men (1-3) — AC 9 (no armour), HD 1, hp 5,3,2, #AT 1, D by weapon, ML 6. Hungry, not organised, exactly what Hask's crew were six days ago. Reaction roll BEFORE assuming a fight.
